research_question_and_rationale: Does predicting the target from surrounding words with CBOW change macro-F1? Skip-gram predicts surrounding words from the target. The objectives can learn different representations from the same token sequences. Lab 8 describes CBOW in cells 60 and 74. Training it is a project adaptation.
tokenization: Lowercase, extract regex word runs, then keep alphabetic tokens only. Keep stopwords and repeats. Apostrophes and hyphens split word runs. No stemming or lemmatization. One token sequence per document.
pooling: Mean of training-vocabulary token vectors, counting repeats. Ignore OOV tokens and use a fixed-width zero vector if no known token remains.
